articles.title: Global Market: Yen speculators turn net long for first time since February
articles.content: Speculators turned bullish on the yen for the first time since February as expectations of faster Bank of Japan rate hikes intensified. Futures positioning swung sharply from net short to net long, reflecting renewed confidence after the currency recovered from a four-decade low.

articles.title: ETMarkets Smart Talk | Retail traders lost ₹1.8 lakh crore in F&O: Can algo trading change the game? Rakesh Pujara explains
articles.content: More than 90% of individual F&O traders lost money between FY22 and FY24, with retail losses reaching around ₹1.8 lakh crore. With algorithmic trading now widespread, automation could help level the playing field by giving retail investors access to tools once largely available to institutions, says Rakesh Pujara of Compounding Wealth Advisors.

articles.title: Global Market: Samsung, SK Hynix reject $18.7 billion upfront power payment proposal
articles.content: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix have rejected KEPCO’s proposal for a 25 trillion won upfront payment to fund electricity infrastructure for planned semiconductor clusters. The move highlights concerns over uncertain chip demand and the significant costs of expanding power infrastructure.

articles.title: Global Market: China stocks mixed, Hong Kong shares edge higher as AI weakness weighs
articles.content: China's mainland stocks traded mixed on Monday as AI and semiconductor shares fell, dragging the CSI AI Index down 1.2% and the STAR50 down 0.9%, even as banking stocks rose due to defensive buying. Hong Kong's Hang Seng gained 0.4%, but its AI sub-index dropped 2.4%, led by a 10.5% plunge in Z.AI after a discounted share placement.

articles.title: Global Market: Japan inflation risks put BOJ rate path in focus
articles.content: Japan’s inflation outlook is becoming increasingly sensitive to import costs, yen movements and supply shocks, raising concerns at the Bank of Japan. Policymakers are assessing whether these pressures could become persistent and influence inflation expectations, as the central bank weighs further rate hikes amid changing domestic and global economic conditions.

articles.title: Jefferies says Sebi's proposed CAS changes will remove uncertainty, but still remains negative on BSE. Here’s why
articles.content: Jefferies expects Sebi’s proposed CAS changes to reduce expiry-day volatility and uncertainty but remains negative on BSE shares, citing limited options-industry growth, a ceiling in market-share gains, tighter bank guarantee norms and a potential management transition. The brokerage prefers Groww, citing strong earnings growth levers and recovery in F&O activity.

articles.title: FIIs sell Indian shares worth Rs 14,475 crore in Sept; analyst warns soaring bond yields may deepen selloff
articles.content: Foreign investors sold Indian equities worth Rs 14,475 crore in September as oil prices and global bond yields surged amid escalating Middle East tensions. Analysts warned that further rises in US Treasury yields could intensify FPI outflows and pressure equities.

articles.title: India beats a hasty retreat from a crucial market reform
articles.content: India’s market-closing auction reform, designed by Sebi to curb price manipulation, has faced volatility and investor backlash within weeks. The regulator may weaken or abandon it, exposing deeper problems: high securities taxes, inadequate arbitrage, shallow liquidity and restrictions on short selling. Poor coordination between fiscal and regulatory policies ultimately undermined reform efforts.

articles.title: US Market: Goldman Sachs expects Fed to hike rates amid inflation fears
articles.content: Goldman Sachs now expects the US Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by 25 basis points in September, reversing its earlier pause forecast. Rising oil prices, stronger producer inflation and shifting market expectations drove the revision.

articles.title: 20 midcap funds, 20 multibaggers: What makes this category a wealth creation machine?
articles.content: Midcap mutual funds have delivered exceptional wealth creation over the past decade, with all 20 schemes boasting a full 10-year track record emerging as multibaggers. But can the category repeat that performance? Experts point to strong earnings growth and structural opportunities, while warning that elevated valuations, volatility, crowded trades and a limited stock universe could constrain future returns.

articles.title: Why can’t NSE trade on its own platform after the IPO, and is it a big deal?
articles.content: NSE MD Ashish Chauhan clarified that the exchange will not seek Sebi approval to list or trade its shares on its own platform. Under Sebi rules, a recognised exchange can list only on another exchange, meaning NSE’s upcoming IPO is expected to result in a BSE-only listing.

articles.title: Commodity Talk| “The conversation is shifting from ‘Can I trade commodities?’ to ‘What role should commodities play?’: Sunil Katke
articles.content: Gold has already established itself as a strategic asset for Indian investors, but the opportunity is increasingly extending to silver, copper and other critical commodities. At the same time, the traditional equity-debt portfolio may not always offer adequate diversification during inflationary or geopolitical shocks, making commodities an increasingly relevant portfolio sleeve rather than simply a trading opportunity.
